bibl.title: Monolithically Integrated μLEDs on Silicon Neural Probes for High-Resolution Optogenetic Studies in Behaving Animals

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: how to deliver light at the scale of a single neuron and record from the same place, in a freely moving animal
span.quote: Despite the rapid advancement of optogenetics in recent years, supporting technology to reliably deliver light to and record electrical signals from deep brain structures in freely moving animals is not readily available.

span.label: whether light sources small enough to match a soma can be built onto a silicon recording probe without excessive heating
span.quote: We report a scalable method to monolithically integrate microscopic light emitting diodes (μLEDs) and recording sites onto silicon neural probes for optogenetic applications in neuroscience. Each μLED and recording site has dimensions similar to a pyramidal neuron soma, providing confined emission and electrophysiological recording of action potentials and local field activity.

span.label: a probe with twelve neuron-sized LEDs and thirty-two recording sites on one silicon shank array, driving spikes at 60 nW and moving the resolution limit from light delivery onto opsin targeting
span.quote: We demonstrate that these “μLED probes” enable control of spiking of single neurons and induce field oscillations of neuronal activity in the intact brain of freely moving mice with unprecedented resolution, so that optical stimulation of a very specific neural circuit is no longer limited by the light delivery methodology, but rather is bottlenecked by the expression specificity of current opsin technologies.

span.label: method
span.quote: This work describes an innovative solution to enhance both spatial resolution and scalability of optogenetic stimulation and recording probes.

span.label: optogenetic light delivery and recording in deep brain structures of freely moving animals
span.quote: Despite the rapid advancement of optogenetics in recent years, supporting technology to reliably deliver light to and record electrical signals from deep brain structures in freely moving animals is not readily available.

span.label: system-or-tool-building
span.quote: We fabricated and implanted the four-shank probes, each integrated with 12 μLEDs and 32 recording sites, into the CA1 pyramidal layer of anesthetized and freely moving mice.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: light reaching non-somatic (dendritic) ChR2 recruits the neuron even when the micro-LED is far from its soma, which smooths the gain-versus-distance relation into a graded rather than step-like profile
span.quote: suggesting that the graded profile of the gain-distance curves ( Figures 4C and S5 ) is due to activation of non-somatic ChR2.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: current flow through the micro-LED raises the voltage of the continuous n-GaN cathode layer, which capacitively couples into the recording interconnects running above it and produces the rectified artifact on all channels
span.quote: we attribute this effect to capacitive coupling from the μLED n-GaN layer to the recording interconnects above: the μLED cathode will experience a finite voltage increase only when there is current.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: excitatory drive arriving at stratum radiatum from CA3 recruits a faster and spatially tighter ripple-generating network than drive arriving at stratum oriens from entorhinal cortex/amygdala
span.quote: suggest that excitatory input at the stratum radiatum (arriving mainly from the CA3) can recruit a faster, more confined network than input to stratum oriens

span.label: coupling an LED into a waveguide is capped by etendue, which is why the light source is put at the site instead of piped to it
span.quote: While LEDs are available at much lower cost and in various wavelengths as compared to laser diodes, the coupling efficiency between an integrated waveguide to the Lambertian emission profile of LEDs is severely limited by the principle of etendue

span.label: silicon is chosen for three separate reasons at once: it can be micromachined into needles, it conducts heat five times better than sapphire, and being opaque it confines emission to one face
span.quote: In contrast to previous approaches using sapphire as the LED microfabrication substrate ( Kim et al., 2013 ; McAlinden et al., 2013 ; Zhang et al., 2003 ), we have designed a process that can monolithically integrate InGaN μLEDs onto silicon substrate to achieve minimally invasive, needle-like shank structures using precise silicon micromachining techniques. Silicon also has approximately five times higher thermal conductivity than sapphire, allowing more effective dissipation of heat generated by the μLEDs ( Mion et al., 2003 ). In addition, having an opaque silicon substrate confines light emission to the topside of the μLEDs, whereas the on-sapphire LEDs can emit light through the transparent probe shanks, leading to poor illumination resolution.

span.label: heat leaves through the shank toward the proximal end, so the most distal LED is the worst case and is the one modelled
span.quote: To build a conservative model, we assumed that all electrical input power is converted into heat. In addition, we only analyzed the temperature increase caused by the most distal μLED (LED1 in Figure S2A ). As illustrated in Figure S2B , the thermal energy generated at the μLED is most effectively dissipated through the thermally conductive silicon probe shank toward the proximal end. Therefore, LED1 generates the greatest temperature rise at any given input power, because the probe tip has the largest thermal resistance to the “heat sink.”

span.label: the graded fall-off of drive with distance implies light is acting on dendrites, not only somata
span.quote: Yet the soma of a single neuron located close to the probe shank is expected to receive very different illumination by distinct neuron-size μLEDs, suggesting that the graded profile of the gain-distance curves ( Figures 4C and S5 ) is due to activation of non-somatic ChR2.

span.label: the artefact has two physically distinct sources - voltage coupling on the board and capacitive coupling from the continuous n-GaN layer - and each has its own fix
span.quote: The second interference component is a rectified waveform that is coupled to all recording channels regardless of which μLED is driven. Because this effect only occurs when there is significant current flowing through the μLED ( Figure S3C ), we attribute this effect to capacitive coupling from the μLED n-GaN layer to the recording interconnects above: the μLED cathode will experience a finite voltage increase only when there is current. This hypothesis is also supported by the observation that the rectified signal is coupled to all recording channels ( Figures S3A and S3C ), as the n-GaN is a continuous layer underneath all recording channels

span.label: Driving the μLEDs induces low-frequency electrical artifacts on the recording channels.
span.quote: A limitation of the current version of μLED probes is the low-frequency artifacts induced during periodic activation.

span.label: Non-somatic opsin expression, not the light source, now caps the achievable spatial resolution of spiking control.
span.quote: The final limitation to the current utility of the μLED probes relates to the available opsin technologies.

span.label: The probe reports spiking only, so it complements rather than replaces intracellular and all-optical methods.
span.quote: Compared to these alternatives, the μLED probe approach is limited in that it only provides information about spiking (and not about intracellular calcium, Vm, or transmembrane currents) and should therefore be viewed as a complementary method.

span.label: The indirect test of heating effects on spike waveforms is weakened by concurrent high-frequency oscillations at high power.
span.quote: However, high-power illumination was occasionally accompanied by high-frequency (2 kHz) oscillations, limiting the interpretational power of these observations.

span.label: photon extraction is poor by construction: 33% internal efficiency, half the light lost into the substrate, most of the rest trapped by total internal reflection
span.quote: These photons generated at the active region are emitted in all directions. Approximately 50% of the photons are emitted toward the substrate and are absorbed at the GaN/silicon interface. Of the remaining photons, only 8.8% can escape from total internal reflection (TIR) at the GaN/brain interface, which has a high index of refraction contrast (n GaN = 2.45 and n brain = 1.36). Additionally, the Ni/Au current spreading layer has 75% measured transparency to blue light. The photon extraction efficiency is therefore only 3.33%, which is similar to results from a previous report

span.label: periodic driving injects a low-frequency artefact into the recordings, present in opsin-free animals and removed only by offline filtering
span.quote: A limitation of the current version of μLED probes is the low-frequency artifacts induced during periodic activation. These artifacts were also observed in opsin-free (wild-type) animals and were removed using offline adaptive filtering ( Figure S3 ). As a result, they did not hinder the analysis of spiking or LFP effects ( Figures 4 , 5 , and 6 ), but limited the range of stimulus waveforms that could be applied.

span.label: there is no accepted safe-temperature standard for implanted devices, so the 1 degree threshold used here is the authors' own
span.quote: As there is no accepted threshold temperature for the safe operation of implantable neural devices ( Elwassif et al., 2006 ), we loosely define the “threshold” as 1

span.label: whether a few milliseconds above 38 degrees harms the adjacent network is stated as unknown
span.quote: Beyond 3.85 V input, the peak temperature can transiently reach 38°C; however, whether a few milliseconds of heating beyond 38°C has adverse effect on the adjacent neural network is unknown.

span.label: the probe reports spiking only, not calcium, membrane potential or currents, and is offered as complementary rather than superior
span.quote: Compared to these alternatives, the μLED probe approach is limited in that it only provides information about spiking (and not about intracellular calcium, Vm, or transmembrane currents) and should therefore be viewed as a complementary method.

span.label: spatial resolution is now limited by where the opsin is expressed rather than by where the light goes
span.quote: The final limitation to the current utility of the μLED probes relates to the available opsin technologies. Non-somatic opsin expression facilitated multilayered control ( Figures 5 and 6 ), but also reduced the spatial resolution of spiking control, resulting in a graded gain-versus-distance profile

span.label: monolithic on-silicon LED fabrication technology is carried over into implantable neural probes for systems neuroscience
span.quote: The monolithically integrated μLED probes described in this work are expected to bridge the gap between the technological advances in semiconductors and advanced applications in systems neuroscience.

span.label: the Pennes bioheat equation, with a blood-perfusion term, is imported to simulate brain tissue heating around the probe
span.quote: Heat transfer physics in the brain with consideration of the μLED heat source and dissipation due to blood perfusion is governed by Penne’s equation

span.label: monolithic integration and lithographic patterning, applied so that light sources and electrodes share one substrate
span.quote: We report a scalable method to monolithically integrate microscopic light emitting diodes (μLEDs) and recording sites onto silicon neural probes for optogenetic applications in neuroscience. Each μLED and recording site has dimensions similar to a pyramidal neuron soma, providing confined emission and electrophysiological recording of action potentials and local field activity.

span.label: etendue, used as the argument for abandoning waveguide coupling altogether
span.quote: While LEDs are available at much lower cost and in various wavelengths as compared to laser diodes, the coupling efficiency between an integrated waveguide to the Lambertian emission profile of LEDs is severely limited by the principle of etendue

span.label: finite-element bio-heat modelling, used to set an operating envelope before any animal was implanted
span.quote: To build a conservative model, we assumed that all electrical input power is converted into heat. In addition, we only analyzed the temperature increase caused by the most distal μLED (LED1 in Figure S2A ). As illustrated in Figure S2B , the thermal energy generated at the μLED is most effectively dissipated through the thermally conductive silicon probe shank toward the proximal end. Therefore, LED1 generates the greatest temperature rise at any given input power, because the probe tip has the largest thermal resistance to the “heat sink.”

span.label: spiking gain here = firing rate during light divided by the same neuron's rate without light, so it is a within-neuron ratio and not a comparison across cells
span.quote: we estimated the location of the soma of each neuron according to the spike amplitude distribution ( Figure 4Ac ) and defined spiking “gain” as the spiking rate during light divided by the rate of the same neuron in the lack of illumination.

span.label: plug efficiency = optical power out over electrical power in; the paper gives both a measured value (0.87%) and a value derived from the loss chain (1.1%), so the measurement is checkable
span.quote: Therefore, the theoretical plug efficiency (P out /P in ) for the μLED is limited to roughly 1.1% by IQE (33%) and extraction efficiency (3.33%) alone.

span.label: iHFO is used exactly as Stark2014 defined it - an induced high-frequency oscillation - and is treated here as a proxy for somatic drive because population synchrony averages out dendritic effects
span.quote: In contrast to single-cell activation, which could be driven non-somatically, the depth profile of the iHFOs may serve as a proxy to somatically confined opsin activation because of the synchronized somatic output of several cells, which can average out the effects of non-somatic opsin drive.

span.label: direct versus indirect activation is a CLASSIFICATION, assigned by a Gaussian mixture model over waveform features, not an observation
span.quote: To distinguish between direct (light) and indirect (circuit) effects, we classified the recorded cells into PYR (directly activated in CaMKII::ChR2 mice due to the paucity of recurrent connections between PYR in CA1; Thomson and Radpour, 1991 ) and interneurons (INT; indirectly activated) using a Gaussian Mixture Model

span.label: the safe threshold is a 1 degree rise, defined by these authors for want of a field standard and described by them as loose
span.quote: As there is no accepted threshold temperature for the safe operation of implantable neural devices ( Elwassif et al., 2006 ), we loosely define the “threshold” as 1

span.label: builds-on → Wu et al., 2013
span.quote: As the first step toward confining light output, our previous work has demonstrated a neural probe with integrated optical waveguide to couple light from an external optical fiber to a microscopic stimulation site ( Wu et al., 2013 ).

span.label: extends → Kim et al., 2013; McAlinden et al., 2013
span.quote: In contrast to previous efforts ( Kim et al., 2013 ; McAlinden et al., 2013 ), we monolithically integrated the μLEDs and recording electrodes on silicon probe shanks, with all dimensions defined with a resolution of < 1 μm.

span.label: extends → Stark et al., 2014
span.quote: Second, we found that focal illumination can generate synthetic CA1 ripples whose properties depend on the locus of the input, extending previous observations during fiber illumination ( Stark et al., 2014 ).

span.label: extends → Stark et al. 2014, by inducing high-frequency oscillations with focal rather than fibre illumination
span.quote: Infra-/intra-layer illumination induced ripples of the highest frequency, which were also most compact in the vertical dimension, while supra-layer (stratum oriens) illumination generated slower and more widespread oscillations ( Figure 6 ). These observations indicate that despite the compactness of the CA1 pyramidal cell layer (~50 μm), multiple ripple generators can reside within the sublayers

span.label: critiques → fibre-coupled optogenetic probes, whose resolution is set by the bulk of the implanted fibre
span.quote: Early work involving in vivo optogenetics relied on manual assembly of commercially available recording components such as metal electrodes ( Anikeeva et al., 2012 ; Gradinaru et al., 2007 ) or passive high-density probes ( Stark et al., 2012 ) with optical fibers, which are bulky and may suffer from misalignment errors. Moreover, the spatial resolution of fiber-based optogenetic devices is limited by the bulk of the implanted fibers.

span.label: critiques → sapphire-substrate microLED probes, which scatter light and cannot be machined into needles
span.quote: However, light scattering from the transparent sapphire substrate and having the recording sites on a separate silicon probe can limit the spatial resolution of the stimulation and recording. In addition, sapphire wafers cannot be micromachined accurately to form needle-like probe structures for minimal insertion damage.

span.label: critiques → injectable polymer LED devices, too wide for cellular resolution and hard to mount on a microdrive
span.quote: Although the flexibility from the polymer substrate can alleviate micro-motion-induced tissue damage, the overall size of the injected components is several hundreds of microns in width (affecting large neuronal groups or entire regions) and is difficult to mount onto micro-drives for post-implantation fine-tuning of the insertion depth.

span.label: confirms → activation thresholds reported for manually assembled diode probes
span.quote: Sub-microwatt (60–120 nW; “low power”) illumination induced time-locked spiking of one or more neurons in the immediate vicinity of the μLED ( Figure 4A ); assuming a neuron-μLED distance of 10 μm, this activation threshold translates to 0.1–0.2 mW mm −2 , values comparable to those observed using manually fabricated diode-probes

span.label: distinguishes-from → two-photon holographic and intracellular methods, which cannot reach deep structures in freely moving animals
span.quote: Such high spatial resolution control over spiking has been previously possible only by intra-cellular current injection or by two-photon microscopy combined with optogenetics ( Packer et al., 2015 ; Rickgauer et al., 2014 ). Intracellular methods are not yet scalable in freely moving animals, while the all-optical approach is not applicable to deep structures in freely moving animals without the destruction of overlying brain tissue.

span.label: μLED —part-of→ silicon
span.note: monolithic integration is the whole claim: the light source is built on the probe rather than coupled to it
span.quote: In contrast to previous approaches using sapphire as the LED microfabrication substrate ( Kim et al., 2013 ; McAlinden et al., 2013 ; Zhang et al., 2003 ), we have designed a process that can monolithically integrate InGaN μLEDs onto silicon substrate to achieve minimally invasive, needle-like shank structures using precise silicon micromachining techniques. Silicon also has approximately five times higher thermal conductivity than sapphire, allowing more effective dissipation of heat generated by the μLEDs ( Mion et al., 2003 ). In addition, having an opaque silicon substrate confines light emission to the topside of the μLEDs, whereas the on-sapphire LEDs can emit light through the transparent probe shanks, leading to poor illumination resolution.

span.label: silicon —contrasted-with→ sapphire
span.note: CRITERION: three at once - machinable into needles, five times the thermal conductivity, and opaque so emission stays on one face
span.quote: However, light scattering from the transparent sapphire substrate and having the recording sites on a separate silicon probe can limit the spatial resolution of the stimulation and recording. In addition, sapphire wafers cannot be micromachined accurately to form needle-like probe structures for minimal insertion damage.

span.label: etendue —causes→ μLED
span.note: a physical invariant is the reason for the design: waveguide coupling cannot be made efficient, so the source moves to the site
span.quote: While LEDs are available at much lower cost and in various wavelengths as compared to laser diodes, the coupling efficiency between an integrated waveguide to the Lambertian emission profile of LEDs is severely limited by the principle of etendue

span.label: plug efficiency —part-of→ internal quantum efficiency
span.note: the measured 0.87% sits just under the 1.1% the loss chain predicts, which is what makes the number checkable
span.quote: Therefore, the theoretical plug efficiency (P out /P in ) for the μLED is limited to roughly 1.1% by IQE (33%) and extraction efficiency (3.33%) alone.

span.label: total internal reflection —causes→ plug efficiency
span.note: SIGN: reduces it. Only 8.8% of upward photons escape the GaN-brain interface
span.quote: These photons generated at the active region are emitted in all directions. Approximately 50% of the photons are emitted toward the substrate and are absorbed at the GaN/silicon interface. Of the remaining photons, only 8.8% can escape from total internal reflection (TIR) at the GaN/brain interface, which has a high index of refraction contrast (n GaN = 2.45 and n brain = 1.36). Additionally, the Ni/Au current spreading layer has 75% measured transparency to blue light. The photon extraction efficiency is therefore only 3.33%, which is similar to results from a previous report

span.label: gain —operationalised-as→ spiking
span.note: direction is measure-to-phenomenon; the ratio is within-neuron, so it cannot be compared across cells of different baseline
span.quote: we estimated the location of the soma of each neuron according to the spike amplitude distribution ( Figure 4Ac ) and defined spiking “gain” as the spiking rate during light divided by the rate of the same neuron in the lack of illumination.

span.label: PYR —contrasted-with→ INT
span.note: CRITERION: PYR are taken as directly driven and INT as circuit-driven, and PYR jitter is lower at every distance
span.quote: To distinguish between direct (light) and indirect (circuit) effects, we classified the recorded cells into PYR (directly activated in CaMKII::ChR2 mice due to the paucity of recurrent connections between PYR in CA1; Thomson and Radpour, 1991 ) and interneurons (INT; indirectly activated) using a Gaussian Mixture Model

span.label: iHFOs —contrasted-with→ ripple
span.note: the induced oscillation is named apart from the spontaneous one, following Stark2014, and its depth profile is read as a proxy for somatic drive
span.quote: Intra-cortical illumination using a μLED close (≤20 μm) to the center of the layer generated iHFOs (frequency range, 85–155 Hz) with power increasing in an intensity-dependent manner

span.label: stratum radiatum —contrasted-with→ stratum oriens
span.note: illumination below or at the layer drives spiking better than above it, attributed to dendritic geometry or expression bias
span.quote: First, we found that illumination of the cell bodies and apical dendrites in the stratum radiatum is more efficient in driving pyramidal cell spiking than stratum oriens illumination ( Figure 4C ). This may be due to a bias in opsin expression and/or to distinct biophysical properties of the large and thick apical (radiatum) and thin basal (oriens) dendrites of the ChR2-expressing pyramidal cells, the former being straight and the latter oblique

span.label: opsin expression —distinct-from→ μLED
span.note: CRITERION: the paper's own claim is that the binding limit has MOVED from the optics to the biology
span.quote: We demonstrate that these “μLED probes” enable control of spiking of single neurons and induce field oscillations of neuronal activity in the intact brain of freely moving mice with unprecedented resolution, so that optical stimulation of a very specific neural circuit is no longer limited by the light delivery methodology, but rather is bottlenecked by the expression specificity of current opsin technologies.

span.label: ChR2 —causes→ spiking
span.note: shown by absence in wild-type controls under the same illumination
span.quote: In CaMKII::ChR2 animals (n = 4; Figure 4 ) but not in control (wild-type, n = 2; Figure S3 ) animals, focal illumination via a single μLED induced spiking of nearby neurons in an intensity-dependent manner.

span.label: rank correlation
span.quote: Resampling (one-sided permutation) tests were used for the testing the significance of rank correlations, and non-parametric testing was used in all other cases.

span.label: permutation test
span.quote: the spiking gain of directly activated PYR depended on both light power (rank correlation: 0.24, p < 0.001, permutation test; 38 PYR yielding 690 cell/power/μLED combinations

span.label: Mann-Whitney U test
span.quote: However, PYR jitter was always lower than the jitter of the indirectly activated INT, both overall (medians: PYR: 29 ms; INT: 46 ms; p < 0.001, Mann-Whitney U test) and for every distance bin (p < 0.01 for all eight bins).

span.label: binomial test
span.quote: At low bias voltages (≤3.1 V), waveforms during light were unmodified (p = 0.3, exact Binomial test

span.label: partial correlation
span.quote: we also computed partial rank correlation between Δμ and ΔS , accounting for P 0 : 0.43, p = 0.001

span.label: principal component analysis
span.quote: Waveforms were linearly detrended, projected onto a common basis obtained by principal component analysis of the data, and sorted automatically

span.label: Gaussian mixture model
span.quote: we classified the recorded cells into PYR (directly activated in CaMKII::ChR2 mice due to the paucity of recurrent connections between PYR in CA1; Thomson and Radpour, 1991 ) and interneurons (INT; indirectly activated) using a Gaussian Mixture Model

span.label: significance level
span.quote: results are reported based on a significance threshold α = 0.05, and all groups included enough samples to enable rejection of the null at that level.

span.label: rank correlation
span.quote: Consistent with the examples ( Figures 4A and 4B ), the spiking gain of directly activated PYR depended on both light power (rank correlation: 0.24, p < 0.001, permutation test; 38 PYR yielding 690 cell/power/μLED combinations; Figure 4C ) and μLED-soma distance (rank correlation: −0.27, p < 0.001; Figure S5B ). A similar pattern was observed for indirectly driven interneurons (INT; rank correlation with light power: 0.32, p < 0.001; with μLED-soma distance: −0.19, p < 0.001; 11 INT, 235 cell/power/μLED combinations; Figure S5 ). Moreover, gain was consistently higher when the μLED was in stratum pyramidale or below the cell body (i.e., in stratum radiatum) than when the μLED was above (i.e., in stratum oriens; rank correlation: −0.23, p < 0.001; Figure 4C ).

span.label: permutation test
span.quote: Consistent with the examples ( Figures 4A and 4B ), the spiking gain of directly activated PYR depended on both light power (rank correlation: 0.24, p < 0.001, permutation test; 38 PYR yielding 690 cell/power/μLED combinations; Figure 4C ) and μLED-soma distance (rank correlation: −0.27, p < 0.001; Figure S5B ). A similar pattern was observed for indirectly driven interneurons (INT; rank correlation with light power: 0.32, p < 0.001; with μLED-soma distance: −0.19, p < 0.001; 11 INT, 235 cell/power/μLED combinations; Figure S5 ). Moreover, gain was consistently higher when the μLED was in stratum pyramidale or below the cell body (i.e., in stratum radiatum) than when the μLED was above (i.e., in stratum oriens; rank correlation: −0.23, p < 0.001; Figure 4C ).

span.label: Mann-Whitney U test
span.quote: However, PYR jitter was always lower than the jitter of the indirectly activated INT, both overall (medians: PYR: 29 ms; INT: 46 ms; p < 0.001, Mann-Whitney U test) and for every distance bin (p < 0.01 for all eight bins).

span.label: Gaussian Mixture Model
span.quote: To distinguish between direct (light) and indirect (circuit) effects, we classified the recorded cells into PYR (directly activated in CaMKII::ChR2 mice due to the paucity of recurrent connections between PYR in CA1; Thomson and Radpour, 1991 ) and interneurons (INT; indirectly activated) using a Gaussian Mixture Model

span.label: Binomial test
span.quote: As an indirect assessment of the heating effect on neuronal activity, we compared the spike waveforms of CA1 pyramidal cells (PYR) during spontaneous activity and during same-shank illumination ( Figure S4 ). At low bias voltages (≤3.1 V), waveforms during light were unmodified (p = 0.3, exact Binomial test; Figure S4A ). Increasing light power caused increased distortion (rank correlation between voltage bias and waveform consistency, −0.2; p = 0.02, permutation test; Figures S4B–S4D ). However, high-power illumination was occasionally accompanied by high-frequency (2 kHz) oscillations, limiting the interpretational power of these observations.

span.label: Sub-microwatt light (60 nW) from a single integrated micro-LED was enough to drive spiking, and microwatt-range power drove fast population oscillations.
span.quote: Spikes were robustly induced by 60 nW light power, and fast population oscillations were induced at the microwatt range.

span.label: The probe achieved independent optical control of neurons roughly 50 micrometres apart and of separate somatic versus dendritic compartments of single neurons.
span.quote: To demonstrate the spatiotemporal precision of parallel stimulation and recording, we achieved independent control of distinct cells ~50 μm apart and of differential somatodendritic compartments of single neurons.

span.label: Illuminating pyramidal cell bodies and apical dendrites in stratum radiatum drove spiking more effectively than illuminating stratum oriens.
span.quote: First, we found that illumination of the cell bodies and apical dendrites in the stratum radiatum is more efficient in driving pyramidal cell spiking than stratum oriens illumination

span.label: Where the light entered the layer changed the induced ripples: infra- and intra-layer illumination produced the fastest and most vertically compact oscillations, while supra-layer illumination produced slower and more widespread ones.
span.quote: Infra-/intra-layer illumination induced ripples of the highest frequency, which were also most compact in the vertical dimension, while supra-layer (stratum oriens) illumination generated slower and more widespread oscillations

span.label: Spiking gain of directly driven pyramidal cells increased with light power and decreased with the distance between the micro-LED and the cell soma.
span.quote: the spiking gain of directly activated PYR depended on both light power (rank correlation: 0.24, p < 0.001, permutation test; 38 PYR yielding 690 cell/power/μLED combinations

span.label: Directly light-driven pyramidal cells spiked with lower temporal jitter (median 29 ms) than indirectly driven interneurons (46 ms), at every distance bin.
span.quote: However, PYR jitter was always lower than the jitter of the indirectly activated INT, both overall (medians: PYR: 29 ms; INT: 46 ms; p < 0.001, Mann-Whitney U test) and for every distance bin (p < 0.01 for all eight bins).

span.label: Thermal simulation showed every drive condition below 3.4 V stays within the 1 degree Celsius safety limit even under ten seconds of continuous DC operation.
span.quote: The result indicates that all operating conditions shown in Figures 3A–3C , which are below 3.4 V, are safe even when the μLED is driven continuously for 10 s.

span.label: 60 to 120 nW of light drove time-locked spiking in neurons next to a single LED
span.quote: Sub-microwatt (60–120 nW; “low power”) illumination induced time-locked spiking of one or more neurons in the immediate vicinity of the μLED ( Figure 4A ); assuming a neuron-μLED distance of 10 μm, this activation threshold translates to 0.1–0.2 mW mm −2 , values comparable to those observed using manually fabricated diode-probes

span.label: two LEDs 60 microns apart controlled distinct neurons independently in freely moving mice
span.quote: Using “low-power” illumination from one of two μLEDs positioned 60 μm apart and thus straddling the CA1 pyramidal cell layer from above and below, distinct neurons could be controlled independently in the intact brain of freely moving mice

span.label: spiking gain rose with light power and fell with LED-to-soma distance for both directly and indirectly driven cells
span.quote: Consistent with the examples ( Figures 4A and 4B ), the spiking gain of directly activated PYR depended on both light power (rank correlation: 0.24, p < 0.001, permutation test; 38 PYR yielding 690 cell/power/μLED combinations; Figure 4C ) and μLED-soma distance (rank correlation: −0.27, p < 0.001; Figure S5B ). A similar pattern was observed for indirectly driven interneurons (INT; rank correlation with light power: 0.32, p < 0.001; with μLED-soma distance: −0.19, p < 0.001; 11 INT, 235 cell/power/μLED combinations; Figure S5 ). Moreover, gain was consistently higher when the μLED was in stratum pyramidale or below the cell body (i.e., in stratum radiatum) than when the μLED was above (i.e., in stratum oriens; rank correlation: −0.23, p < 0.001; Figure 4C ).

span.label: directly driven pyramidal cells had lower spike jitter than indirectly driven interneurons at every distance
span.quote: However, PYR jitter was always lower than the jitter of the indirectly activated INT, both overall (medians: PYR: 29 ms; INT: 46 ms; p < 0.001, Mann-Whitney U test) and for every distance bin (p < 0.01 for all eight bins).

span.label: illumination inside or below the layer produced faster and more compact induced ripples than illumination above it
span.quote: Infra-/intra-layer illumination induced ripples of the highest frequency, which were also most compact in the vertical dimension, while supra-layer (stratum oriens) illumination generated slower and more widespread oscillations ( Figure 6 ).
